initialFindings.issue: AD-10's withdrawal/deposit formula contradicts its no-new-headroom cycle invariant. With a 1,000 NOK monthly plan, no deposits and opening goal balance 100, S=1,000. Withdraw 100 and redeposit 100 in the same month: goal balance is restored, S remains 1,000, but W=100 permanently increases A by 100. The savings service can correctly record both transactions while the calculation service correctly applies the written formula and manufactures headroom.
initialFindings.fix: Define one explicit treatment for redeposits of released goal money, including within-plan deposits, and amend W/S together so a completed withdrawal/redeposit cycle restores A. Add this exact scenario alongside an ordinary withdrawal and a deposit exceeding plan. Keep the resulting rule proposed for human acceptance.

initialFindings.issue: AD-5 binds all history and defines historical cash result as I minus E minus actual deposits, but AD-10 excludes debt and annual-fund payments from E and adds W separately. A reporting unit obeying AD-5 omits actual debt/fund outflows and savings withdrawals; a ledger unit obeying AD-10 correctly classifies them separately. The same year therefore reports different cash result depending on which contract is followed. AD-10 calls A an extended formula but never supersedes the historical cash-result definition.
initialFindings.fix: Explicitly scope AD-5's simple A formula to the core projection and make AD-10 the authoritative expanded calculation. Define the signed historical cash-result projection across every actual posting class, including refunds and withdrawals, separately from allocations/reservations; include an example with a fund-funded payment and debt payment. Update the capability map's reporting references.

initialFindings.issue: AD-6 requires every paid occurrence to create one linked expense and puts paid bills in category consumption (AD-5), while AD-10 requires linked debt/fund occurrences to point to their single non-E-class posting. A generic bills implementation can obey AD-6 by creating an ordinary expense, while debt/fund modules obey AD-10 by creating their own payment, resulting in two effects or a class conflict. The exception and dispatch ownership are not expressed in the shared payment command contract.
initialFindings.fix: State that the bill payment command creates exactly one posting whose class comes from the occurrence's ordinary/debt/fund obligation type; ordinary postings alone enter E, with debt/fund settlement delegated atomically to their respective rules. Define whether category actuals include each class, and apply the same dispatch to undo/refund without creating a second posting.

initialFindings.issue: AD-4 permits historical effective-date corrections and AD-10 allows withdrawal up to available goal balance, but it does not define available balance as of the withdrawal date or the validity of later events after correction. A goal service can check today's balance under a lock and accept a September withdrawal against an October deposit; a historical reporting service then reconstructs a negative September goal balance while still obeying the date rules. The dated opening balance creates the same seam if used before its effective date.
initialFindings.fix: Specify an effective-date balance rule for withdrawals/opening balances and a minimal rule for later withdrawals made invalid by editing/deleting earlier funding. Validate the affected chronological goal history atomically, or explicitly prohibit those mutations until a correction flow is agreed; add one backdated withdrawal example.
